profile.name: Sandee Srisawat
profile.headline: Building the systems behind the play.
profile.intro: I’m a game programmer interested in creating responsive gameplay, reusable systems that connects, to create memorable player experiences.
profile.about: I’m interested in the details that make a game feel good to play: responsive controls, thoughtful interactions, and systems that work together.
profile.approach: This space is for my story: how I approach a difficult problem, what I enjoy building, and what draws me to game programming. I’ll add that story alongside my work.

projects.title: Excorcism Of Elizabeth
projects.description: A space to explain enemy behavior, decision-making, or an interconnected gameplay system.
projects.overview: This is a sample project breakdown, ready for a real project. The prompts below describe what to add; they do not represent completed work or experience.
contributions: Designed and implemented a modular player interaction system using a BPI_Interactable Blueprint Interface and a BPC_PlayerInteractor Actor Component, enabling any actor in the world to become interactable without modifying the player character.

Built a two-handed inventory system with pick up, drop, item mesh swapping, and hand-specific slot tracking, structured to work correctly in a multiplayer environment using Server RPCs and replicated variables.
Designed a time-based event system using BP_TimeManager and BP_BasedTimedActors, allowing world actors such as doors and magic circles to trigger and respond to timed gameplay events.

projects.challengesTakeaways: The biggest challenge was making the interaction system work in multiplayer. Calls made directly from the client on world actors get silently dropped by Unreal since the client doesn't own them. I solved this by moving the Server RPC onto the player's own component, which then calls the interface on the item from the server. This taught me how Unreal's ownership model works and why multiplayer architecture needs to be considered from the start.
